newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI listing gives mkt mid-term lift-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI listing gives mkt mid-term lift-Salomon.

text.p: The June 12 listing of National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme will likely stimulate foreign interest and buoy the bourse in the mid-term, Salomon Brothers in London said in a report.
"Medium-term market benefits are likely from the increase in depth as a result of NIF listings," the Emerging Europe Strategy report said, giving Poland and overweight rating.

Salomon also said this year's remaining heavy privatisation schedule, highlighted by the June-July offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz, would deepen the market, broaden its industrial base and could draw new global investors.

It said Poland's economic growth, which Salomon sees at 5.5 percent this year after last year's 5.6 percent, helped the country have, from a macroeconomic perspective, "the healthiest economy in the region."
But Salomon said parliamentary elections, due September 21, would bring added uncertainty to the market.
Current polls show the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the rightist opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) with about 25 percent support each.
"A win by the right-wing parties will probably stall reform and may reduce foreign investments in Poland," the report said.
